key_insight: Sparse-QITE uses regularization to discover compact QITE generators, cutting circuit depth and gate count while preserving high ground-state accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical path to lower-resource quantum simulation by reducing both gate execution cost and measurement overhead in QITE workflows.
method: Add sparsity-promoting regularization to the local Pauli generator fit.
Select a compact subset of Pauli terms to approximate imaginary-time updates.
Use adaptive regularization and active discovery to further reduce measurements.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on 1D transverse-field Ising and antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models show a controllable sparsity–accuracy trade-off, with some large-domain cases using about 1% of the standard-QITE gate count after transpilation.
watch_item: Performance depends on regularization tuning and problem structure, so overly aggressive sparsification could reduce accuracy or limit transferability across models.
paper_title: Sparse-QITE: Discovering Compact Generators for Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution via Regularization Methods
